title: Speaking Sweet Words
note: This means saying sweet words that show the gladness in your mind. Those who care for guests can’t do without it, so it follows that chapter.

couplets.plain: Sweet words are what come from the mouths of those who have seen the truth: steeped in tenderness and free of deceit.
couplets.pm: Sweet words are the words from the mouths of those who know righteousness, mixed with loving-kindness and free of deceit. To mix them is to show loving-kindness, and to be free of deceit is to be true. Righteousness is called the straight thing because it seems straight to all who know the truth. “Mouths” shows they never practise evil words.

links.quote: steeped in tenderness and free of deceit

couplets.plain: Better than giving with a glad heart is to have a glad face and sweet words.
couplets.pm: Better than gladly giving someone what they need is to have a pleasant face the moment you see them, and sweet words with it. Unlike giving, this depends on you and not on wealth, yet it doesn’t come naturally except to those with righteous hearts, so it is rarer.

links.quote: to have a glad face and sweet words

couplets.plain: Righteousness lies in a glad face, a kind look and sweet words that come from the heart.
couplets.pm: On seeing someone, welcome them with your face and look on them kindly. Then, when they come near, say sweet words from the heart. Righteousness lies in that, not in giving. These two couplets say a pleasant face with sweet words wins people over at once, and so comes first in caring for guests.

links.quote: sweet words that come from the heart
links.reason: Finds righteousness itself in a sweet word from the heart.

couplets.plain: The poverty that brings sorrow will not come to those whose sweet words bring joy to everyone.
couplets.pm: Poverty, which increases sorrow, won’t come to those whose sweet words increase everyone’s joy. Poverty is the senses lacking what they would enjoy. Such people have no enemies and no strangers, only friends, and so gain all wealth.

links.quote: sweet words bring joy to everyone
links.reason: Promises that poverty will not reach those whose sweet words bring everyone joy.

couplets.plain: Humility and sweet words are a person’s ornaments. Nothing else is.
couplets.pm: A person’s ornament is to bow to those one should bow to and to have sweet words for all. The other ornaments worn on the body aren’t ornaments, because they don’t give such beauty. Humility is named because it goes with sweet words. These two couplets tell the reward of sweet words in this life.

links.reason: Puts humility first of the only two things that truly adorn a person.
Pairs sweet words with humility as a person’s whole finery.

couplets.plain: If you seek out what is good and say it sweetly, wrongs will wear away and righteousness will grow.
couplets.pm: If you weigh in your mind words whose meaning does others good, and say them sweetly, your sins wear away and righteousness grows. Sin wastes away because its enemy, righteousness, is growing and it has no footing. Even what is good isn’t righteousness if it is said harshly. This tells the reward in the next life.

links.reason: Says sweet words, joined with seeking the good, make wrongs wear away.

couplets.plain: Words that are useful and never part from courtesy give rise to fairness and bring good.
couplets.pm: Words whose meaning does others good, and which never lose their sweetness, bring the speaker justice in this life and righteousness in the next. Justice means being in accord with the world. Courtesy here means sweetness.

links.quote: Words that are useful and never part from courtesy

couplets.plain: Sweet words free of all meanness bring joy in the next life and in this one.
couplets.pm: Sweet words that cause others no pain by their meaning give you joy in both worlds. The next life is named first because its joy is greater. Joy in this life is gaining good things, because the world is on your side. These two couplets stress that both rewards come together.

links.quote: bring joy in the next life and in this one

couplets.plain: If you have seen what joy sweet words bring, why use hard words?
couplets.pm: Someone who has felt the joy that others’ sweet words give him: what does he hope to gain by speaking hard words to others? Hard words are unpleasant to others too, so they shouldn’t be said.

links.reason: Asks why anyone who knows the better way would still use hard words.

couplets.plain: To speak harsh words when sweet ones are there is like picking unripe fruit when ripe fruit is there.
couplets.pm: To say harsh words that bring sin, when you have sweet words that bring righteousness, is like eating bitter unripe fruit when sweet ripe fruit is in your hand. The ripe fruit is like ambrosia and the unripe like poison. Harsh words end by hurting the one who says them. These two couplets tell the fault of harsh words.

links.quote: To speak harsh words when sweet ones are there

links.reason: Sweet words are what the harsh speaker leaves hanging on the tree.

links.quote: picking unripe fruit when ripe fruit is there

ideaLinks.quote: The poverty that brings sorrow will not come
ideaLinks.reason: Poverty never comes to those whose sweet words bring everyone joy.
Sweet words, with a search for the good behind them, make righteousness grow.

ideaLinks.quote: To speak harsh words when sweet ones are there
